reply_text:
Reading Goguen's own definition of a blend before I write anything on it; the first PDF came out garbled, so I'm trying the other copies.Still on Goguen's formal definition: the text extraction failed, so I'm reading the appendix pages of the PDF directly.Sources read; now writing the v3 draft beside the 1 October file, with Goguen's definitions cited by page, then sending it to claude-17 and codex-10 for comment.㊥ ("It's a blend with emergent structure") Taken as settled. I found and read the Goguen details you did not remember, in his own papers rather than from memory, and they answer the one question claude-17 had left open: pasting does hold for his weakened pushouts, so a cascade is a blend at larger scale even with emergent structure. I have written the amendments as a v3 draft beside the 1 October file (futon2 `265ab6253`) and sent it to claude-17 and codex-10 for comment. You did not say yes to the draft, only to the pushout question; it is one file, marked draft, and easy to drop.

㊢ ("Goguen 1-and-a-half categories") The source is Goguen's "An Introduction to Algebraic Semiotics" (1999), Appendix B, now filed with checksums in `wm-contract/refs/`. Its text layer is garbled, so I read the four pages by eye. What it says:
- **A 3/2-category** is a category whose arrows between two objects are partially ordered, by quality: one map is above another when it preserves at least as much content, every axiom the other does, and is as inclusive. He calls them "one and a half" categories in a footnote.
- **A 3/2-pushout** keeps the shape of a pushout but replaces "exactly one mediating map" with "a best one": among the maps from the blend to any other candidate blend, there is a maximum.
- **Non-uniqueness is the point.** "Two different 3/2-pushouts need not be isomorphic; this means that ambiguity is natural in this setting."
- **Pasting holds.** The composition of two 3/2-pushouts is a 3/2-pushout, a 2×2 grid of them is one, and the colimit of any connected diagram can be built from them. One caution: pasting two consistent squares can give an inconsistent figure, so consistency has to be checked.
- **Names matter.** Isomorphic cones do not represent the same blend, because which element goes to which is part of the blend.

㊢ ("a houseboat and a boathouse") His 2006 paper gives the full example. From house and boat he lists six blends: houseboat, boathouse, a boat that carries houses, an amphibious RV, a livable boat for transporting livable boats, and a boat used on land as a house; the Alloy program found 42 more, "most of which are far from optimal". He also writes that for this example "the most natural blend is an ordinary pushout, all the other good blends are 3/2-pushouts, and various blends that fail to preserve as much structure as they could are not any kind of pushout". Only houseboat has all its triangles commuting; the others have what he calls auxiliary maps.

㊢ ("emergent structure") Two statements of his, five years apart: in 1999, that the quality order itself "captures what Fauconnier and Turner have called emergent structure, without needing any other machinery"; in 2006, a hypothesis that emergent structure arises by recruiting an extra space that matches concepts the inputs mention but the common ground did not integrate. Read against construction, the second is a rule for where an extension candidate comes from. I put it in the draft as open, not as a rule.

㊢ (what the draft says, in brief)
1. The unit is a square: two inputs, what they share, and the blend, each recorded as text with its source, supplied by a reading of the pattern for the problem. No slot mapping, on the evidence of the sample.
2. v2's three relations are derived: support is a leg into a blend; a meet is the shared object under two occurrences, named as text and required only where two occurrences are glued; precedence is two orders kept apart, construction order forced and application order evidenced. v2's rule against simultaneity from a missing edge stands.
3. Occurrences that share nothing are a bag, reported as such. The last click's cascade is a bag by this rule.
4. Same inputs with different maps are different policies, which is your requirement Q10 in Goguen's words.
5. Five added Lean obligations, including finite witnesses of non-uniqueness and of inconsistent pasting.
6. Left open: how the quality order enters G; the relation to the existing co-application kernel; which parts of a library pattern are the inputs.

㊬ (one check in the library) None of the 109 patterns that state an axis shares a pole with another, so the library has no houseboat/boathouse pair written as such.

㊯ (in flight) claude-17 and codex-10, comments on the draft; each asked to check the quotations against the PDF pages, and codex-10, as v2's author, to say where v3 misreads v2. Jobs `invoke-1791237356680-33164-1ef923ba` and `invoke-1791237359862-33165-a3585ac9`; parks `park-3eb21c09-6a00-4343-8b9c-4d8ed2c33ced` and `park-0f36ee68-526b-4859-8c53-97268f3ac418`.

Sources: [Goguen, Algebraic Semiotics (PDF)](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~goguen/pps/as.pdf), [Goguen, Mathematical Models of Cognitive Space and Time (PDF)](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~goguen/pps/taspm.pdf), [Goguen, Notation for Conceptual Blending](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~goguen/courses/271sp01/blend.html)

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("a design pattern is itself a conceptual blend, i.e. a pushout") My reading, for you to correct. A pattern is a square: two inputs, what they have in common, and the blend that both map into. My guess at the slots, which is mine and not yours: IF and HOWEVER are the two inputs, the context is the common ground, THEN is the blend, and BECAUSE is the warrant that the blend honours both and adds nothing else.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
("when these are combined you get a cascade") What I think follows from that:
1. **One pattern is already a diamond.** The common ground sits under both inputs and the blend over both. A list or a tree cannot hold even one pattern.
2. **Patterns combine by sharing parts.** One pattern's blend is another's input or common ground. Squares pasted this way are again a pushout, so a cascade is a blend at a larger scale and a single pattern is the smallest case.
3. **The draft's three relations come from one construction.**
   - Support is an arrow from an input into the blend it helps form.
   - A meet is the common ground of the square in which two patterns are the inputs.
   - Precedence is partly forced, because a blend cannot be formed before its inputs and common ground exist.
4. **Meets are needed only where patterns are glued**, which is the semilattice condition, not a meet for every pair.
5. **Patterns with nothing in common form only a disjoint sum.** The last click's cascade is nearly that: four patterns, each picked separately for one want, with one dependency. Almost nothing in it was blended, so it has almost no shape.
6. **Shared parts are counted once.** The 30 September note on G as a fold left open how a shared part is counted once; here the shared part is the common ground, and the pushout identifies it a single time.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(where I am unsure)
- **The slot mapping.** I do not know that IF and HOWEVER are the inputs.
- **Precedence.** Point 3 derives part of it from structure. The draft says precedence must not be inferred from support. These may be two different orders, forming a blend versus applying it to a problem, or they may conflict.
- **Free energy.** I have not worked out what this account says about G beyond point 6.
